note: The IRB of Canada's 2016 response (DJI105552.FE, read 2026-11-03 on the IRB's own site and on ecoi.net): the digital identity card (introduced by the 2014 reform) is issued by the Ministry of the Interior's Population Branch to citizens of 18 and over, and (the 2017 response adds) cannot be applied for or obtained outside Djibouti; the Branch's own website, as the IRB read it in 2016, gave DJF 2,700 for a first card and DJF 2,000 for renewing one, and the card's term, ten years. Until then the card was held at DJF 2,000 for everyone, the procedural fee the Director of Population and Family gave La Nation (2014) for exchanging the old card, which the same response quotes; the first card is now 2,700 and the renewal 2,000. The Branch's site (lapopulation.dj) wasn't reached; the time isn't stated.

sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, DJI105552.FE, Djibouti: Requirements and procedure to follow to obtain a national identity card (31 August 2016), the IRB's own copy of the response ecoi.net reprints
sources.said: Similarly, the website of the Population and Family Branch states that the issuance fees for renewing an identity card are 2,000 DJF, but that they are 2,700 DJF for individuals being issued the card for the first time (Djibouti n.d.b). ... a representative of the Embassy of Djibouti in Washington stated that national identity cards are issued to citizens aged 18 and up (Djibouti 29 June 2016). ... Djibouti. N.d.b. Direction générale de la population et de la famille. “La carte d’identité numérique est valable dix ans, mais, même périmée, elle permet à son titulaire de justifier de son identité sur le territoire national, à condition que la photographie soit ressemblante.” [Accessed 5 July 2016]
